report:
Reviewed the complete handle_ownership claim and all three ordinary implementation entries and eight ordinary tests. There are no TODO/N/A entries. Requirements are (1) Ptr and Slice have stash-local interpretation, (2) retaining values across ownership boundaries uses recursive structural copying, and (3) completed checked trees retain no source-CST or imported-result stash handles. Captured storage-guide.md lines 1–39 makes the first requirement a valid-use ownership invariant with debug identity diagnostics, explicitly documenting compact release handles; it does not promise release-mode rejection of same-type misuse. Index validates identity in debug and type in all configurations. I do not claim release identity enforcement.

Implementation: sage-stash/lib.rs constructs stash-local handles and validates their owner on indexed access in debug. Stashed::copy_into delegates to StashCopy; Ptr reads from source, recursively copies its value, then allocates in target; Slice copies each element recursively before target allocation; Option maps recursive copying and direct leaves copy as values. The associated macro implementation generates recursive field copying for named/tuple structs and enum variants, with units copied directly. These are the essential copying implementation files and both are associated. finalize.rs creates a fresh stash, recursively rebuilds all type, expression, pattern, statement, call-target, field, closure and match-arm pointer/slice edges, resolves transient type/expression references before retaining them, memoizes copied nodes, and packages only destination allocations in TyBodyData. Captured ty.rs and tytree/mod.rs show all pointer/slice-bearing fields handled by those exhaustive cases; LocalVar contains name/span only. Captured types.rs establishes TokenTree is a Salsa tracked identity marked StashDirect, not a stash pointer, so its direct retention is valid. Source layouts are captured dependencies rather than independent copying implementations.

Tests: cross_stash_ptr_same_type_panics_in_debug and cross_stash_slice_panics_in_debug visibly access another stash at a matching index and expect the identity panic in debug; they provide no release identity assertion. cross_stash_ptr_wrong_type and cross_stash_slice_with_different_element_type_is_rejected expect identity panic in debug and type panic otherwise. copy_into_compound checks both nested pointer referents and copy_into_with_slice checks both copied slice elements. copied_nested_handles_survive_source_drop_and_destination_growth supplies a deliberately different destination layout, drops the source, allocates 4096 more values, and asserts the scalar, all three nested slice referents, and repeated-child identity; shallow copying or retained source offsets would fail those checks. finalized_nested_body_owns_resolved_and_imported_types_after_sources_drop copies an imported Boolean type into transient input, finalizes nested tuple expressions with resolved inference types, drops the source/import/egraph, and traverses the completed destination alone, asserting types, literal values, spans, empty locals, lengths and sharing. The test's source offset perturbation and debug owner validation expose retained source handles. Together these assertions cover pointer/slice ownership, nested structural copying and completed-output independence, rather than relying on names or association markers.

Executed cargo test -p sage-stash --test arena_tests --test storage_contracts: 46 arena tests and 9 storage-contract tests passed, including every associated stash test. Executed cargo test -p sage-ir finalized_nested_body_owns_resolved_and_imported_types_after_sources_drop --lib: the one selected ownership test passed (70 filtered out). No release tests were run; release behavior statements above are source inspection. No production or test code was changed. No unresolved behavioral concern or required edit remains.
